done_when: src/forge/fasttest.py is simpler and none of these happen any more: Cap worker counts supplied through pytest configuration; Exclude unrelated tests explicitly named by the full command; Recognize source-prefixed paths and package-relative imports

findings.body: When `tests/test_unrelated.py` is excluded, a valid command such as `pytest tests --ignore tests/test_unrelated.py -q` loses the value following `--ignore`. Pytest then rejects the modified command before running any tests. Whitespace-separated `--ignore-glob` and `--deselect` values have the same problem, including node IDs because this filter strips `::` suffixes. These are [pytest options requiring values](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytest-dev/pytest/9.1.1/src/_pytest/main.py). Remove excluded positional collection arguments while preserving option/value pairs.
findings.title: Preserve option values when removing explicit test paths

findings.body: At this hook, `early_config.option.maxprocesses` still contains its default, not the client's parsed setting. [Pytest 9.1.1 stores the parsed options in `known_args_namespace` before invoking this hook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytest-dev/pytest/9.1.1/src/_pytest/config/__init__.py). Consequently, on an eight-core machine, `-n auto --maxprocesses=1` gets an appended `--maxprocesses=4` and starts four workers. This also overrides smaller limits from pytest configuration and `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`, in both focused and full-fallback runs. Read the parsed limit from `known_args_namespace` before taking the minimum. This preserves the coordinator's hook-based approach while addressing the newly verified parsing-order issue.
findings.title: Honor an existing worker limit below the machine cap

why: Simplify src/forge/fasttest.py: problems keep turning up there
